dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Big Flower Hand 大花糊 is the rarest luck in the game: you draw all eight flower tiles.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Flowers are bonus tiles. You set each one aside and draw a replacement straight away, so your hand never grows.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: And eight of them just sits at the top of the chart?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: It is a limit hand, so it settles at 10 faan, which is 128 points off a discard.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Seven flowers is the smaller cousin, 小花糊, worth 3 faan, and holding all four seasons or all four flowers is 一台花 for 2.

questions.question: How many faan is Big Flower Hand 大花糊 worth?
questions.explanation: 大花糊 is a limit hand, and every limit hand is scored at the 10-faan ceiling.

questions.question: How many flower tiles must you draw to make Big Flower Hand 大花糊?
questions.explanation: The set has four seasons plus four flowers, so collecting all eight of them is the hand.

questions.question: You draw seven flowers instead of eight. What does that pay, and does self-draw add anything?
options: 小花糊, 3 faan, with no self-draw faan added
小花糊, 4 faan with the self-draw faan
Nothing, because seven flowers does not count
questions.explanation: 小花糊 is 3 faan for seven flowers, and the rules do not add a self-draw faan to it.

questions.question: Put the four season flowers in seasonal order, starting from spring.
questions.explanation: The seasons run spring, summer, autumn, winter, and all four together make 一台花.

questions.question: You already hold {{f_plum}} {{f_orchid}} {{f_chrys}}. Which tile completes the four-flower set for 一台花?
questions.explanation: The flower set is plum, orchid, chrysanthemum and bamboo, so 竹 is the missing fourth tile.

questions.question: Match each flower holding to what it is worth.

pairs.left: All four seasons, or all four flowers

questions.explanation: The chart runs from 1 faan for no flowers up to the 10-faan limit for the full eight.

questions.question: A 大花糊 is won by self-draw. How much does each of the other three players pay?
questions.explanation: At 10 faan a self-draw is 64 from each player; the 128 figure is what a single discarder would pay.

questions.question: Which statements about flowers are true?
options: A drawn flower is set aside and you draw a replacement tile
Eight flowers is 大花糊, a 10-faan limit hand
A flower tile can be used as a triplet inside your hand
questions.explanation: Flowers are never part of the hand, so they cannot form a triplet; the other three statements match the chart.

14-2.title: All Terminals & Honours
14-2.subtitle: 花么 — ones, nines and honours only

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: All Terminals and Honours 花么 is a small hand with a very big family tree.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Every tile must be a one, a nine, or an honour tile. Nothing in between is allowed.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: Then I cannot make a chow at all, can I?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Right, which is why 花么 always arrives with 對對糊. That is 1 faan plus 3, so 4 in total.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Do not confuse it with 清么九, which is ones and nines only, or 字一色, which is all honours. Both are 10 faan.

questions.question: The 花么 pattern on its own is worth how many faan?
questions.explanation: 花么 is a 1-faan pattern; the 對對糊 it forces is counted separately on top.

questions.question: Which tiles may appear in an All Terminals and Honours 花么 hand?
options: Ones and nines of the three suits only
Any tile, as long as no chow is used
questions.explanation: 花么 allows every terminal and every honour, but no tile from two to eight.

questions.question: Why does 花么 always count as 對對糊 as well?
options: Because a chow cannot be built from terminals and honours, so every set is a triplet or kong
Because 花么 hands must be concealed
Because the pair must be an honour pair
Because 對對糊 is automatically added to any 1-faan hand
questions.explanation: A chow needs three consecutive numbers, and none of them can be a terminal or an honour, so only triplets and kongs remain.

questions.question: Adding the 對對糊 to the 花么 pattern, how many faan does the hand collect in total?
questions.explanation: 1 faan for 花么 plus 3 faan for 對對糊 gives 4 faan.

questions.question: Which of these tiles could never appear in a 花么 hand?
questions.explanation: A five of characters is a middle tile, and 花么 only permits ones, nines and honours.

questions.question: Match each hand to its value.

pairs.left: 花么 pattern on its own
花么 together with 對對糊
清么九 or 字一色

questions.explanation: 花么 is a 1-faan pattern that drags 對對糊 along for 3 more, while the two pure versions are limit hands.

questions.question: A 4-faan hand is completed on a discard. How much does the discarder pay?
questions.explanation: On the payment table 4 faan is 16 points from the discarder, who pays the whole amount alone.

questions.question: Which statements about these three hands are true?
options: 花么 may contain honour tiles
清么九 may contain honour tiles
字一色 contains no suited tiles at all
花么 always brings 對對糊, so it is worth 4 faan
questions.explanation: 清么九 is ones and nines with no honours; the other three statements describe 花么 and 字一色 correctly.

14-3.title: Rob the Kong
14-3.subtitle: 搶槓 — stealing the fourth tile

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Rob the Kong 搶槓 is the art of stealing a tile that someone has just turned into a kong.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: Normally it happens on an added kong 加槓, where a player tops up their own pung with the fourth tile.

dialogues.speaker: you
dialogues.text: And if that fourth tile is exactly what I need to win, I just take it?

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: You do, for 1 faan, and the player who made the kong pays your whole self-draw amount on their own.

dialogues.speaker: mj
dialogues.text: One more twist: 十三么 is the only hand allowed to rob a concealed kong.

questions.question: What exactly is Rob the Kong 搶槓?
options: Winning on the tile an opponent adds to their kong
Winning on the last tile of the wall
Winning on the tile you draw to replace a flower
Winning on a tile that you discarded earlier yourself
questions.explanation: 搶槓 is claiming a kong tile as your winning tile, not a wall draw or a flower replacement.

questions.question: Which kong can normally be robbed?
options: Only a kong of honour tiles
questions.explanation: The usual target is the added kong, because the fourth tile is placed openly on an existing pung.

questions.question: Which hand is allowed to rob a concealed kong?
questions.explanation: 十三么 is the single exception that may rob a concealed kong; every other hand needs an added kong.

questions.question: How many faan does 搶槓 add to a hand?
questions.explanation: 搶槓 is listed as a 1-faan item, and it stacks with whatever the rest of the hand is worth.

questions.question: An opponent upgrades their exposed {{s6}} {{s6}} {{s6}} pung by adding the fourth {{s6}}, and {{s6}} is your winning tile. Which tile do you claim?
questions.explanation: You claim the exact tile added to the kong, which here is the fourth 六索.

questions.question: A 4-faan hand is completed by robbing a kong. Who pays what?
options: The player whose kong was robbed pays all 24 points alone
All three players pay 8 points each
Nobody pays, because a kong is not a discard
questions.explanation: A robbed kong is treated as a self-draw paid as a package: the robbed player covers the whole 24-point self-draw total for 4 faan.

questions.question: Match each term to its description.

pairs.left: The kong that is normally robbable
The hand allowed to rob a concealed kong

questions.explanation: 搶槓 scores 1 faan, targets an added kong by default, and only 十三么 may go after a concealed one.

questions.question: Which statements about 搶槓 are true?
options: 搶槓 is scored as 1 faan
The robbed player pays the whole self-draw amount alone
The other two players split the rest between them
A concealed kong can only be robbed by 十三么
questions.explanation: The robbed player is treated as the package payer and covers everything, so the other two pay nothing.
